quote: Beweise, dass die Bernoullische Function irre= ducibel ist.
english: Prove that the Bernoulli function is irreducible.
topic: Three short notes: proving that the Bernoulli function (polynomial) is irreducible, using its behaviour modulo a prime degree p; a remark that an ideal probability device (wheel of fortune) is impossible; and a task to set up a theory of calculation.

triage.modern_statement: Show that the Bernoulli polynomials B_n(x) = Σ_k C(n,k) b_k x^(n−k) are irreducible over Q. Hilbert's hint seems to be to look at B_n mod p when the degree n = p is prime, which is an Eisenstein- or p-adic-type argument. Taken literally for every n, the statement is false: for odd n ≥ 3, B_n(x) has the trivial factors x, (x−1/2) and (x−1). The real question is therefore whether the even-index B_{2m}(x) are irreducible over Q, and whether the odd-index B_{2m+1}(x) divided by x(x−1/2)(x−1) are irreducible. One caveat: I am assuming that Hilbert's 'Bernoulli function' means these Bernoulli polynomials (the page summary calls it a polynomial). He may instead have meant a closely related polynomial, such as the sum-of-powers polynomial.
triage.answered_by: Not fully answered. Partial results: L. Carlitz, 'Note on irreducibility of the Bernoulli and Euler polynomials', Duke Math. J. 19 (1952), 475–481, proved B_n(x) irreducible for n = k(p−1)p^r with 0<k<p, using p-adic (Eisenstein-type) methods. P. J. McCarthy, H. Kimura and A. Adelberg later strengthened and extended these results, and Adelberg also worked on higher-order Bernoulli polynomials. J. Brillhart (Crelle 234, 1969) studied the factorisation, and Brillhart and Dilcher proved that Bernoulli polynomials are squarefree. The general irreducibility of the even Bernoulli polynomials is still described as a long-standing conjecture (e.g. arXiv:1607.08418, 2016).

evidence.claim: Carlitz (1952) proved that B_n(x) is irreducible when n = k(p−1)p^r with 0<k<p. McCarthy and Kimura later strengthened this using Eisenstein-type conditions.
Reference for Carlitz, 'Note on irreducibility of the Bernoulli and Euler polynomials', Duke Math. J. 19 (1952), 475–481.
A 2016 paper calls the irreducibility of the even Bernoulli polynomials a long-standing conjecture, and cites the Brillhart–Dilcher theorem that Bernoulli polynomials are squarefree.
Brillhart, 'On the Euler and Bernoulli polynomials', J. Reine Angew. Math. 234 (1969), 45–64, studies the factorisation and irreducibility of these polynomials.
Survey of Carlitz's theorem on odd m and related indecomposability results for B_m(x).
There is follow-up work on the irreducibility of higher-order Bernoulli polynomials (Canad. J. Math. vol. 14) and of generalized Bernoulli polynomials (J. Number Theory 1987).

triage.why: The note matches a well-known question: are the Bernoulli polynomials irreducible over Q? Carlitz proved special cases in 1952 using p-adic/Eisenstein arguments, which fits Hilbert's 'mod prime degree p' hint, and Brillhart, McCarthy, Kimura and Adelberg extended them. The full statement for the even Bernoulli polynomials is still cited as an open, long-standing conjecture in recent papers. It is not one of Hilbert's 23 problems or the 24th problem, and I found no source linking Hilbert to it. Confidence is medium because the note is very short and 'Bernoulli function' could refer to a related polynomial.
